features.title: Western delta · water-altered clays
features.evidence: Orbital spectra identify clay and carbonate minerals in layered delta sediments. These minerals are consistent with water–rock alteration and sediment deposition in an ancient lake system.
features.interpretation: Orbital spectral detection and regional geologic interpretation
features.keyPoint: Layered delta sediment contains Fe/Mg smectite and carbonate signatures.
features.whyItMatters: Clay-rich sediments can preserve chemical traces of water and potential biosignatures.

features.title: Western delta · hydrated silica detection
features.evidence: A CRISM spectral detection near the western delta has absorption features consistent with hydrated silica. The published detection is regional and the marker indicates its approximate area.
features.interpretation: CRISM detection verified from extracted spectra
features.keyPoint: Hydrated silica was detected in a western-delta outcrop.
features.whyItMatters: Silica can preserve fine-scale biosignature evidence; the detection helps prioritize a science stop.

features.title: Paleolake margin · carbonate-bearing unit
features.evidence: A carbonate-bearing unit follows part of Jezero’s inner margin near the western delta and a major inlet. Researchers propose that some of these carbonates may have precipitated in a near-shore paleolake environment.
features.interpretation: Published interpretation; lacustrine origin is a hypothesis
features.keyPoint: Carbonate-bearing rock traces part of the crater's inner margin.
features.whyItMatters: If it formed at the lake shore, this unit could preserve environmental clues from the paleolake.

features.title: Margin Unit · eastern campaign area
features.evidence: Perseverance measurements in the eastern Margin Unit report carbonate-rich rocks, silica, and localized veins with calcium sulfate and fluorite. The NASA waypoint at sol 925 is used as an approximate campaign location; the minerals are not all present at that single point.
features.interpretation: Rover measurement campaign, with representative waypoint at sol 925
features.keyPoint: Eastern Margin Unit carbonate estimates reach about 6–16 wt% in the studied rocks.
features.whyItMatters: The chemistry suggests repeated groundwater and possibly lake-related alteration; localized veins also point to later fluid flow.

features.title: Western delta · ancient water evidence
features.evidence: A fan-shaped deposit with layered sediments records river transport into a former lake. This is geological evidence of ancient surface water, not a present-day water spot.
features.keyPoint: Layered fan deposits mark a river entering an ancient lake.
features.whyItMatters: The layers record how water and sediment moved, helping select safe, scientifically useful Marswalk destinations.

features.title: Northern delta · hydrated silica detection
features.evidence: CRISM analysis verified a second hydrated-silica detection near the northern Jezero delta. The coordinate is an approximate map location for the published detection area.
features.interpretation: CRISM spectral detection verified from extracted spectra; approximate location
features.keyPoint: A second silica-rich detection occurs by the northern delta.
features.whyItMatters: Seeing silica in two delta settings suggests more than one place may preserve clues to ancient water and habitability.

features.title: Crater floor · Al-phyllosilicate detection
features.evidence: CRISM spectral analysis reported an Al-phyllosilicate detection in Jezero. Its plotted location is approximate because the paper identifies the detection in a regional figure rather than providing a ground-station coordinate.
features.interpretation: CRISM detection verified from extracted spectrum; approximate map location
features.keyPoint: A distinct aluminum-rich clay signature occurs in Jezero.
features.whyItMatters: Different clay chemistry can record different water conditions and alteration histories.

features.title: Séítah · weakly altered olivine-rich floor
features.evidence: Perseverance studied olivine-rich Séítah rocks near its landing area. The recent multi-instrument synthesis estimates roughly 1–3 wt% carbonate in this unit, lower than in the Upper Fan and Margin Unit.
features.interpretation: Rover unit-scale synthesis; landing waypoint used as approximate unit location
features.keyPoint: Séítah is olivine-rich and comparatively weakly altered, with about 1–3 wt% estimated carbonate.
features.whyItMatters: It provides a baseline for comparing how much more strongly water altered later units.

features.title: Fan Front · Shenandoah formation
features.evidence: Perseverance's Fan Front campaign investigated the lower western fan. Published mapping describes the Shenandoah formation as fine- to medium-grained sedimentary layers, with sulfate and clay minerals dominating the analyzed primary mineralogy. Location is represented by a nearby sol 663 waypoint.
features.interpretation: Rover campaign geology with a representative sol 663 waypoint
features.keyPoint: Fine sediments and sulfate/clay signatures occur in the lower fan.
features.whyItMatters: These deposits help reconstruct flowing water and lake conditions at the delta front.

features.title: Upper Fan · Tenby outcrop
features.evidence: SuperCam and other Perseverance instruments detected carbonate-bearing rocks in Upper Fan outcrops including Tenby. The wider Upper Fan unit has estimated carbonate contents around 3–9 wt%; the map point is a nearby sol 732 waypoint, not a target pixel.
features.interpretation: Rover campaign synthesis with representative sol 732 waypoint
features.keyPoint: Upper Fan rocks contain more carbonate than Séítah and preserve tilted delta beds.
features.whyItMatters: The bed geometry and carbonate chemistry connect water-laid sediments with water–rock alteration.

features.title: Upper Fan · Otis Peak formation
features.evidence: The Otis Peak formation contains coarse sandstone and conglomerate interpreted as fluvial topsets in the delta sequence. A nearby sol 784 rover waypoint marks this approximate visited area.
features.interpretation: Rover-observed sedimentary unit with representative sol 784 waypoint
features.keyPoint: Rounded pebbles and coarse beds record energetic water transport.
features.whyItMatters: Clast size and rounding help estimate ancient flow strength and distinguish river deposits from quiet lake sediments.

features.title: Margin Unit · western-most area
features.evidence: In the studied western-most, highest part of the Margin Unit, Perseverance observations show weaker alteration dominated by Fe/Mg phyllosilicate rather than carbonate. The coordinate is a nearby sol 1100 waypoint.
features.interpretation: Rover campaign synthesis with representative sol 1100 waypoint
features.keyPoint: The western-most Margin Unit is clay-dominated and has less carbonate evidence.
features.whyItMatters: The east-to-west mineral change shows alteration varied across the unit instead of affecting every rock equally.

features.title: Neretva Vallis · ancient channel corridor
features.evidence: Perseverance traversed Neretva Vallis, a channel that once carried water into Jezero. The marker uses a NASA sol 1206 waypoint in the rover's channel-crossing campaign.
features.interpretation: Mapped ancient channel and rover traverse waypoint
features.keyPoint: This valley was an inlet route for water and sediment into Jezero.
features.whyItMatters: Channel deposits link the crater lake to its watershed and offer another place to compare transported minerals.
